mentions.name: Easel
mentions.description: A programming language that teaches teenagers to code by making multiplayer games. Multiplayer is fully automatic: games are coded like singleplayer projects and can be switched to multiplayer with no extra work. It uses rollback netcode for low latency across continents, and a matching system described as a mix of Roblox and Scratch. Region affinity is being implemented so players aren't all placed in one shared world.
mentions.problem: Making multiplayer games is traditionally difficult, so the project automates it completely; latency across continents is handled with rollback netcode, but the game world is currently too large to put everyone in the same game, motivating region affinity.
mentions.audience: Teenagers learning to code, who can play the games they make with their friends
mentions.source_excerpt: A programming language for teenagers to learn to code by making multiplayer games. I've spent 3 years making the multiplayer completely automatic so you can just code it like a singleplayer game, then flick a switch and it just works. My hope is that teenagers will find it more engaging if they can play their games with their friends. A bit like a combination of Roblox and Scratch.
